subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be defined around live gateway runtime health, passive local plugin status, or the current `not checked` mitigation for normal/deep status?
rationale: Current main avoids one misleading word but does not implement the requested live-runtime health contract, and the remaining fix changes the status/doctor boundary for plugin-owned memory runtimes.

options.title: Use live gateway runtime health
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Define a passive local status contract
options.body: Keep memory details local only if plugins get a clearly passive status API that cannot start heavyweight runtime work and has third-party regression coverage.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as enough
options.body: Declare current status wording sufficient, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue only after documenting why live runtime health is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway runtime health
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits place the memory runtime, status snapshot, and gateway doctor memory surfaces under vincentkoc's active area work.
